priorities.name: Quiet, private space for focus and confidential work
priorities.issue: Associates cannot reliably find quiet or private space for concentrated work and confidential conversations; even managers with designated space report having to leave their seat for a booth. This is the site's single largest driver of dissatisfaction.
whatItLooksLike: even with designated manager/director space, there is still minimal privacy and sensitive conversations require you to get up and move to a privacy booth which is inconvenient and disruptive.
Working at a pulse point is challenging due to potential missing items and high noise levels.

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (89/100).
Friction for focused individual work is 37/100 — 64% under-supported; discretion 27/100 (50% under-supported).
Noise & Distraction: 105 people (27% of respondents), 137 comments, 74% negative. Privacy & Confidentiality: 75 people (19% of respondents), 100 comments, 62% negative.
Reserved seats lose value when the surrounding environment doesn't support the work done there.

priorities.proposedAction: Assess current quiet/phone-booth/enclosed-room capacity against peak demand; determine whether booking limits, an etiquette/quiet-zone protocol, or added enclosed capacity is the right fix before proposing construction.
priorities.siteMustDo: Walk the floor at peak occupancy, log where and when private/quiet space runs out, compare with booth/room utilization, and escalate a capacity gap to Workplace Solutions with evidence.

priorities.name: Desk reservation reliability and arrival readiness
priorities.issue: Desk reservations and the state of reserved workstations don't consistently hold up, so associates lose time getting set up when they arrive.
whatItLooksLike: Often cords or mouses are missing from desks and I do not know who to contact

evidence.text: Desk Availability & Reservations: 66 people (17% of respondents), 84 comments, 57% negative — the 5th most-raised theme by people (it was the highest-volume theme before the November 2026 re-tag, which stopped counting every mention of a desk).
Physical Environment is the #2 priority category (68/100).

priorities.proposedAction: Review booking rules and no-show behavior, and stand up a clear, visible path for reporting a desk found missing equipment on arrival.
priorities.siteMustDo: Audit a sample of reservations against actual occupancy for two weeks, confirm the failure mode (double-booking vs. no-shows vs. setup), and post the who-to-contact path at each neighborhood.

priorities.name: Workstation equipment reliability
priorities.issue: Monitors, cords and peripherals at shared desks are frequently missing or misconfigured, interrupting work.
whatItLooksLike: The limited availability of capsule rooms with dual monitors. There are times I have presentations to facilitate, and I cannot find an empty capsule room (others working in them for longer than an hour.) and pods do not have monitors in…

evidence.text: Hardware (Monitors / Peripherals): 74 people (19% of respondents), 98 comments, 65% negative.
A recurring per-desk reliability issue rather than a one-off failure.

priorities.proposedAction: Institute a routine equipment check for shared workstations and standardize the docking/monitor setup so any desk works the same way on arrival.
priorities.siteMustDo: Inspect a sample of workstations, catalog missing/broken peripherals and reset-monitor issues, and set a recurring check with Technology.

priorities.name: Thermal comfort (temperature)
priorities.issue: Temperature is uneven across the floor — some desks run cold, especially in summer — so associates plan their day around which desk they can get.
whatItLooksLike: Sometimes the temperature is set to too cold and everyone on the floor is freezing especially in Summer time. …
Temperature control is difficult so depending on what desk I am able to secure I need to plan accordingly.
Temperature can be an issue, can be too cold and uncomfortable.

evidence.text: Temperature / Thermal: 36 people (9% of respondents), 40 comments, 68% negative.
Thermal / temperature comfort: Under Supported — friction 19/100 (41% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Have Workplace Operations map the cold zones by floor and time of day, then check set-points, airflow balancing and diffuser placement in those zones before considering any equipment change.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log cold desks/zones and times for two weeks, submit them to building operations, and re-check after each adjustment to confirm it holds.

priorities.name: Meeting-room and video-conferencing reliability
priorities.issue: Laptop connections, audio and screen-sharing in conference and meeting rooms fail intermittently, which undermines the client and hybrid meetings the rooms exist for.
whatItLooksLike: I have found that many of the conference room connections do not work well. They have been treated rough and when I connect my laptop sometimes they connect and disconnect intermittently. It is unreliable.

Some of the meeting rooms do not function reliably. There are often connectivity issues, audio frequently cuts in and out during meetings, and several rooms lack accessible power outlets for charging laptops. …
…Some conference rooms when you directly connect your laptop to share screens you lose your internet connection. …

evidence.text: Video conferencing & meeting-room technology agreement: 3.58 vs 3.72 company average (Moderate) — close to the 3.5 'Needs attention' line.
Virtual collaboration with remote/hybrid colleagues: Under Supported — friction 20/100 (39% under-supported).
Meeting & Conference Rooms: 35 people (9% of respondents), 45 comments, 58% negative; AV / Video Conferencing: 14 people (4% of respondents), 14 comments, 64% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Have Technology test every conference and huddle room end-to-end (laptop connection, display, audio, camera, power), repair or replace worn cables and connectors, and post a short in-room quick-start guide.
priorities.siteMustDo: Run a room-by-room test with Technology, log failures by room, and re-test the repaired rooms after 30 days.
